clue.text: Fashion on the street is unpretentious

parts.note: a fashion or vogue is a mode

explanation.surface: A remark that fashion seen out on the street is plain and unshowy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone modest is humble and unassuming, without airs or pretension.

clue.text: Talk or alternatively, eat

indicators.note: alternatively suggests the three letters of the next word arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone offered the choice of making conversation or tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is taken as written; 'alternatively' rearranges EAT into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length, a formal or pompous way of talking.

clue.text: Hair removal offered — that is, with lipo and tan treatments

indicators.note: treatments suggests the letters being worked over into a new form

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A beauty salon menu offering liposuction and tanning along with waxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatments' shuffles IE, LIPO and TAN together; 'offered' and 'with' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilation is the cosmetic stripping of body hair at the root, by waxing or laser.

clue.text: Mongols say goodbye with hollow regards

parts.note: ta-ta is a British informal way to say goodbye

indicators.note: hollow means the word regards is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes leave with only half-hearted good wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties REGARDS to its first and last letters, RS. Ta-ta is a casual British farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars were Turkic peoples of the Mongol hordes, so the name is used loosely for Mongols.

clue.text: An old song, "crazy about a girl"

parts.note: crazy means mad

indicators.note: about here means the letters of the next two words are scattered around

explanation.surface: A song title in quotation marks, a lover besotted with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the phrase look like a song title, but 'about' is the anagram signal working on the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for several unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: The greatest guarantee prison offers

parts.note: read literally as the strongest assurance available, but it names the strictest category of jail regime

explanation.surface: A claim about the best promise a jail can make.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both the largest possible guarantee and the label for the toughest high-security prisons.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest category of jail confinement, for the most dangerous inmates, is known by this term.

clue.text: Scorns hell — dad took insurance against it!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, hence hell
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A child mocks the idea of hell because father has taken out cover against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdaining something means looking down on it with contempt.

clue.text: Order I take on, being in charge

explanation.surface: A command, I accept the duty since I am the one in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is not a command here but a classical architectural order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, with scrolled column capitals.

clue.text: American visits English hills and Italian mountains

parts.note: the Pennines are the range of hills running down northern England

explanation.surface: A US tourist touring hills in England and then mountains in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visits' just links the A to the hills. The Pennines are the upland backbone of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the range forming the spine of the Italian peninsula.

clue.text: The capital state of film production

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France, the archetypal capital
Texas is a US state

explanation.surface: A question about which capital or state is home to the film industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film production' is the definition: a 1984 Wim Wenders film whose title joins the city and state.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris, Texas is a 1984 road movie by Wim Wenders, a film production of note.

clue.text: In turnip production, Nebraska takes the record

parts.note: NE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nebraska
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Farm news: Nebraska tops the league for growing root vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'production' set the agricultural scene and give no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scottish word for a swede or turnip, served with haggis.

clue.text: Figure he will cross a good ram

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A farmer will breed his ewes with a fine ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like the breeding verb but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexagram is a geometric shape, a six-pointed star formed from two triangles.

clue.text: The secret of sugar cane extraction

indicators.note: extraction says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about the hidden technique for getting sugar from the cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane matters are mysterious, known only to the initiated.

clue.text: Musical in which American soldiers meet French girl

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier; two of them give the plural
GI is again an American soldier

explanation.surface: A show in which GIs encounter a young Parisian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The French girl is the title heroine of the musical, from Colette's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is the 1958 Lerner and Loewe film musical about a young Parisienne.

clue.text: Not lively — in a lively way

parts.note: animate means lively or full of life

explanation.surface: A contradiction: being dull, and yet doing it with spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a playful split: read in two pieces, the answer seems to say 'in an animated manner', the opposite of its real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate has no life or movement, like a stone.

clue.text: Naming EC when disaster is threatening

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Naming the European Community when things go wrong is ominous.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing behaviour is intimidating and suggests harm to come.

clue.text: Fighter requires hairdresser to be at worker's disposal!

parts.note: a comb is something that dresses hair
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A man needs a hairdresser always available to a member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairdresser' is not a stylist but the tool that dresses hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is someone taking part in fighting, a soldier or warrior.

clue.text: An account to believe and show to be true

parts.note: A/C is the standard abbreviation for an account
to credit a story is to believe it

explanation.surface: A ledger entry that one is asked to trust and verify.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit a claim is to vouch for it or certify it officially.

clue.text: Sea creature, type of lean crab

indicators.note: type of hints that the next words take another form, the letters regrouped

explanation.surface: A marine animal said to be a kind of thin crab.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle is a marine crustacean that clings to rocks and ship hulls.

clue.text: Acorns provide this tall timber

explanation.surface: A description of an oak, from its seeds to its towering trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the fallen nuts of forest trees such as beech and oak; it is also a tall pole on a ship carrying sails.

clue.text: Made an asinine row!

parts.note: seems to describe someone causing a foolish quarrel, but asinine is meant literally: the noise a donkey makes

explanation.surface: Someone kicked up a stupid fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey braying makes its loud harsh call, literally an ass's din.

clue.text: Cook left out dieter

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is dropped from the word for dieter

parts.note: a slimmer is someone on a diet

explanation.surface: A chef has been excluded from the meal plans of someone on a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To simmer food is to cook it gently just below boiling.

clue.text: A real grind to prepare such food

definitions.text: A real grind to prepare such food

parts.words: A real grind to prepare such food
parts.note: a real grind sounds like a tiresome chore, but the food is literally ground up

explanation.surface: A complaint that some dish is laborious to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat is chopped or ground into small pieces in a grinder.

clue.text: Peacekeepers' motive is nonsense

parts.note: the UN supplies international peacekeepers
a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: A claim that the United Nations' cause is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is irrationality, the absence of sense or logic.

clue.text: Communist can look back when more mature

indicators.note: back tells us the whole run for the communist and the look is read in reverse

parts.note: a red is a Communist
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A Communist is able to reminisce once he grows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REDLO to make the answer; 'can' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone older has more years behind them, so is further along in life.

clue.text: First four out of eighteen go into store

indicators.note: first four out of means only the opening letters of the referenced answer are kept

parts.note: eighteen refers to the answer to 18 across

explanation.surface: The leading four runners from a field of eighteen go into the warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eighteen' is the answer to 18 across, the sea creature; keep its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm building used to keep grain, hay or produce.

clue.text: Mary said I'd corrupted farm-girls!

indicators.note: corrupted suggests the words before it are spoiled and their letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Mary has claimed to lead astray some country lasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairymaids were young women employed on farms to milk cows and make butter.

clue.text: Not long ago, you could depend on us currency investment

indicators.note: investment is read as putting something inside, the coin placed within the word for depend

parts.note: to depend is to rely
the cent is a unit of US currency

explanation.surface: Financial advice: a sound US dollar investment is something you can trust.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'us' is really US, the United States, and 'investment' signals one piece going inside another, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time just past.

clue.text: Silly old fool's marriage portion is a small road

parts.note: dot is an old legal term for a dowry, from French
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A dowry turning out to be only a little lane makes the giver look foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is someone feeble-minded through old age.
